title: Marc-André ter Stegen Joins Ajax on Season-Long Loan From Barcelona
excerpt: The 34-year-old German goalkeeper heads to Amsterdam after losing his starting spot at Camp Nou, with Barcelona covering the bulk of his €15 million salary.
body:
• Ajax confirmed the signing of Marc-André ter Stegen on a one-season loan from Barcelona on Tuesday.
  • Barcelona will continue paying 75-80% of ter Stegen's approximately €15 million annual salary, with Ajax contributing less than €2 million.
  • The German goalkeeper reunites with coach Míchel, who managed him briefly at Girona last season, and works alongside Ajax sporting director Jordi Cruyff.
  • Ter Stegen is part of a broader Ajax summer rebuild that includes Julian Brandt, Tolu Arokodare, and Marcos Leonardo.

Ajax Amsterdam have completed the loan signing of goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen from Barcelona, the Dutch club announced on Tuesday. The 34-year-old arrives on a one-season deal, ending weeks of protracted negotiations over salary terms and tax complications.

The move marks a significant chapter change for a goalkeeper who spent 12 seasons at Camp Nou, making 423 appearances and winning 20 trophies, including seven La Liga titles and the 2015 Champions League. Ter Stegen had fallen behind Joan García and veteran Wojciech Szczęsny in Barcelona's goalkeeping hierarchy under head coach Hansi Flick.

A Deal Built on Relationships

Ajax sporting director Jordi Cruyff, who previously held the same role at Barcelona, was instrumental in bringing the deal together, according to ESPN. Cruyff's familiarity with ter Stegen from their shared time at the Catalan club helped smooth negotiations that at times appeared stuck.

https://x.com/DeadlineDayLive/status/2084544132878377174

The goalkeeper will also be reunited with Ajax head coach Míchel, who briefly worked with him at Girona during a loan spell last season. That stint lasted only two appearances before a hamstring injury ended ter Stegen's campaign and cost him a place in Germany's World Cup squad.

"Ter Stegen's desire has been key. The 34-year-old wants to join the Dutch club and work under Míchel."

— Jijantes, via SPORT

As a ball-playing goalkeeper known for his distribution, ter Stegen fits the patient, possession-based style Míchel wants to implement at Ajax, according to ESPN's Sam Marsden and Moises Llorens.

Barcelona Shoulder the Financial Burden

The financial terms underscore Barcelona's eagerness to find ter Stegen regular playing time, even at considerable cost. According to Soccerway and multiple Spanish outlets, Barcelona will continue paying between 75 and 80 percent of the goalkeeper's annual salary of approximately €15 million. Ajax are expected to contribute less than €2 million.

The deal does not include an option to buy, meaning ter Stegen will return to Camp Nou at the end of the season. Barcelona did negotiate performance-based bonuses into the agreement, including clauses tied to appearances and Champions League qualification, according to Soccerway.

Barcelona's portion of the salary will not be fixed but will vary depending on how much ter Stegen plays — a condition Ajax insisted on after Girona's experience last season, when Barcelona paid their full share despite the goalkeeper featuring only twice due to injury, according to Mundo Deportivo.

Part of a Broader Ajax Rebuild

Ter Stegen's arrival is part of an ambitious summer recruitment drive at Ajax. The club also signed former Borussia Dortmund midfielder Julian Brandt, 30, on a free transfer to a three-year deal last week. Nigerian striker Tolu Arokodare joined on loan from Wolverhampton Wanderers, while Brazilian forward Marcos Leonardo arrived from Al Hilal for just under €20 million on a five-year contract, according to Reuters.

Clubs from England, Germany, and Turkey had also expressed interest in ter Stegen during the transfer window, but none advanced as far in negotiations as Ajax, ESPN reported.

What's Next

Now fully recovered from the hamstring injury that derailed his Girona loan, ter Stegen will look to re-establish himself as a first-choice goalkeeper and rebuild his international career. For Ajax, a Champions League-winning keeper with over 400 top-flight appearances represents a statement signing as Míchel reshapes the squad ahead of the new Eredivisie season.

Ter Stegen's contract with Barcelona runs until 2028. Whether this loan serves as a stepping stone toward a permanent exit or a route back to relevance at Camp Nou will likely depend on his performances in Amsterdam over the coming months.
